input.strategy_title: Keyboard accessibility conformance for core Dashboard flows
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

An accessibility audit found that four core Dashboard flows (project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run submission) cannot be completed
with keyboard alone: focus is lost in modals, several controls are unreachable,
and focus indicators are inconsistent. Two public-sector customers require an
updated, published conformance statement (VPAT) before renewal — so the fixes
and the published documentation are both deliverables of this strategy.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard, with no focus traps or unreachable controls. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited flows. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect the fixed state, with technical review. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Screen-reader semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require
- Flows outside the four audited ones

## Open Questions

None — the audit report enumerates the exact defects per flow.

# Keyboard accessibility remediation for the four audited Dashboard flows

## Description

This epic makes the four audited core Dashboard flows — project creation,
workbench spawn, model deployment, and pipeline run submission — fully operable
with keyboard alone, and makes visible focus indicators consistent across
those flows. It resolves every defect enumerated in the accessibility audit
report for these flows: focus loss in modals, controls unreachable via
keyboard, and inconsistent focus indicators.

## Scope

- Remediate each defect enumerated in the accessibility audit report across
  the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment,
  pipeline run submission):
  - Fix focus handling in modals so focus is not lost — focus enters the modal
    when it opens, remains trapped within it while it is open in the tab
    order, and returns to the triggering control when it closes.
  - Make every interactive control in the audited flows reachable and
    operable via keyboard (tab order, arrow-key navigation where the control
    type expects it, Enter/Space activation, Escape to dismiss).
  - Apply a single consistent visible focus-indicator treatment across all
    interactive controls in the audited flows, replacing the current
    inconsistent indicator styles.
- Out of scope per the strategy: screen-reader semantics beyond what the
  keyboard fixes require, and any flows outside the four audited ones. Any
  audited defect whose resolution would require out-of-scope semantics is
  dispositioned with a recorded rationale rather than silently dropped.
- The Dashboard's existing build pipeline and CI must remain green with these
  changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the four audited flows (project creation, workbench spawn, model
  deployment, pipeline run submission) can be completed end-to-end using the
  keyboard alone, verified by a recorded keyboard-only walkthrough of each
  flow.
- Every defect enumerated in the audit report for these flows is resolved, or
  explicitly dispositioned as out of scope with a recorded rationale.
- No focus traps remain: opening and closing any modal in the audited flows
  moves focus into the modal and returns it to the triggering control.
- No unreachable controls remain: every interactive control in the audited
  flows is reachable via keyboard and operable without a pointing device.
- A single focus-indicator treatment is applied consistently across all
  interactive controls in the audited flows (no per-page or per-flow indicator
  variations).
- The Dashboard's existing build pipeline is green with the changes included.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P1)**: The four audited core flows are fully operable by keyboard,
  with no focus traps or unreachable controls.
- **HLR-2 (P1)**: Visible focus indicators are consistent across the audited
  flows.

# Update and republish accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and accessibility statement)

## Description

This epic updates and republishes the accessibility conformance documentation
— the VPAT (Voluntary Product Accessibility Template) and the product docs
accessibility statement — so it reflects the fixed state of the four audited
Dashboard flows once the keyboard accessibility remediation is complete. The
published conformance statement is a customer-facing deliverable: two
public-sector customers require it before renewal.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Update the VPAT so its conformance claims for keyboard operability and focus
  visibility reflect the actual fixed behavior of the four audited flows
  (project creation, workbench spawn, model deployment, pipeline run
  submission).
- Update the product documentation accessibility statement to reflect the
  current accessibility state, including any remaining known limitations
  outside the four audited flows and outside keyboard scope (screen-reader
  semantics beyond what the keyboard fixes require are out of scope for the
  fixes and must be stated accurately as limitations where relevant).
- Republish both artifacts through the standard Red Hat documentation content
  process so the updated conformance statement is publicly available.
- Every conformance claim must trace to a verified, shipped fix — no claim may
  assert behavior beyond what the implementation delivers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The VPAT is updated so that each keyboard-operability and focus-visibility
  claim accurately reflects the implemented behavior of the four audited
  flows, with no claim that overstates the shipped state.
- The product docs accessibility statement is updated and republished.
- Each conformance claim in the updated VPAT traces to a specific verified
  fix in the audited flows (claim-to-fix traceability recorded).
- The updated documentation has been technically reviewed against the
  implementation (keyboard accessibility remediation of the audited flows) and
  the review sign-off is recorded before republication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P2)**: The accessibility conformance documentation (VPAT and
  product docs accessibility statement) is updated and republished to reflect
  the fixed state, with technical review.
